rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's fourteen builder trees go (a row of magnolias and jacarandas along the back fences, a norfolk pine and a queen palm 3 m from the house fronts, others in the yards); five come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the two swing sets, the adirondack chair, the open lot corner, and one on the old back fence row.

trees.why: the back yard with the swing set (2.8 m off): shade over the swings
the south yard with the swing set (2.8 m off): a young eucalyptus over the swings
the yard with the adirondack chair (1.7 m off): a coral tree to sit under
the open lot corner at the south-east, 22 m from the walls: a full jacaranda
the west end of the north back fence row, 5.4 m from the house: the row's one tree (it had one every 6-20 m)
